title: Invert CI so language layers own their own jobs
description:
ci/github in the bailiff catalog holds 60 questions, 44 of which exist only to answer which languages the repo has. The language layer already knows.

Move wc-lint-<lang>.yml, wc-test-<lang>.yml, and actions/setup-<lang>/ out of the host layer into each lang/* layer. The host layer keeps wc-changes, wc-gate, wc-quality, wc-security and the ci-gate action.

Every conditional filename in ci/ disappears, since inclusion follows from which layer rendered.
acceptance_criteria: templates/host/github declares no language question. Adding a language touches one directory. A rendered repo has exactly the workflows its layers contributed.
close_reason: CI inversion works end to end and was unblocked once psc-20v closed. Each lang/* layer ships its own wc-lint-<lang>.yml, wc-test-<lang>.yml, setup action, and .github/{quality,security}.d fragments; the host layer's wc-quality and wc-security build their matrices at run time by reading those directories, so adding a language contributes jobs without touching the host layer or a caller. Verified across five language layers plus iac/terraform, iac/cdk, container/image, and lang/api.

title: Port the 161 template files into layers
description:
The bailiff catalog at ~/personal/dev/bailiff/.apm/skills/bailiff/packages/ holds 161 template files across 30 packages. They are the tested content and port as-is; the parameterisation does not.

Source groups map to layers: foundation -> base, languages -> lang, ci -> host/github, repo -> host + release, hooks -> quality, workspace -> workspace, agentic -> agentic, iac -> iac, docs -> docs.

Fold each package's questions down to the fixed preferences in rules/choices.md. Of 247 questions, roughly 170 disappear.
acceptance_criteria: Every template file present under templates/, each layer renders standalone against a fixed answer set, and no layer declares a question that rules/choices.md marks fixed or derived.
notes:
Layer design is in docs/layers.md: 19 layers, ~34 variables. Per-language file shape is fixed (tool configs, .gitignore.d, .pre-commit.d, .mise/conf.d, .just.d, wc-{lint,test}-<lang>.yml, setup-<lang>, .gitlab/ci/<lang>.yml).

Two destination roots per language layer in a monorepo: member dir for tool configs and .pre-commit-config.yaml, repo root for mise/just/CI fragments.

.gitignore.d fragments shrink to conditional lines only -- gitnr covers /target, __pycache__, node_modules already. What it cannot express: Cargo.lock ignored for lib but committed for bin, vendor/ under Go vendor mode.
close_reason: Port complete. Every layer the bead listed exists and is verified by rendering plus running the real tool: host/{github,gitlab}, quality/hooks, workspace/{monorepo,just,moon,devcontainer}, release/{release-please,cocogitto,dep-updates}, agentic/{apm,package,beads,index,rtk,speckit,marketplace}, docs/{agents,adr,site,deploy-sibling,deploy-split}, iac/{terraform,cdk}, container/image, lang/{rust,python,go,ts,api}. 34 layers, 13 profiles, 568 tests, just check green. docs/api-refs is the one item deferred to its own bead (psc-2yu), since it needs docs/deploy-split's split topology. title: Add the agentic/package layer
description:
A self-publishing agentic-package repo: the shape shared by break-stuff and clerk (one package under packages/<name>, the repo is its own marketplace). Distinct from agentic/apm, which configures a CONSUMER of packages.

Verified against apm 0.26.0:
- targets: [claude, codex, kiro]; kiro is a real deploy target (.kiro/), used in ~/work/dev repos. It is NOT a marketplace.outputs key -- only claude and codex have mappers (source: apm_cli/marketplace/output_profiles.py). apm rejects kiro: {} under outputs.
- marketplace.outputs codex requires category: on every package.
- Each package needs its own apm.yml or --check-versions reports [no_apm_yml].
- tagPattern must match release-please: include-component-in-tag: true <-> {name}--v{version}, tag-separator: --.
- apm pack builds root marketplace.json (.claude-plugin/ and .agents/plugins/) but does NOT materialise per-package .claude-plugin/plugin.json or .codex-plugin/plugin.json. For the single-package shape these are rendered statically from answers rather than generated.
- --check-clean only gates with --dry-run (else it regenerates before diffing); --check-versions never verifies a tag exists.

Writes: apm.yml (marketplace block), packages/<name>/{apm.yml, .apm/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json}, release-please-config.json + manifest, .just.d/package.just (marketplace-build/-check recipes wrapping apm pack), .gitignore.d/apm. Like agentic/apm, it runs no apm pack at render time; a just recipe does.

Verify by rendering and running apm pack --offline against the result, then apm pack --check-clean --dry-run.
close_reason: Ported and verified against apm 0.26.0. Single self-publishing package shape (break-stuff/clerk). targets claude+codex+kiro, marketplace.outputs claude+codex only (kiro has no mapper). Per-package plugin manifests rendered statically since apm pack does not create them. Both claude+codex and claude-only paths render and apm pack cleanly; --check-clean --dry-run gate proven to catch drift and plain --check-clean proven to miss it. 17 tests, 330 total, just check green at 5eec3ad.

title: Give SpecKit its own layer instead of apm package locators
description:
SpecKit is being rearchitected, and it is important enough to warrant its own layer rather than three apm package locators.

CURRENT STATE (as of 2026-07-29): SpecKit exists nowhere in templates/. It appears only as prose:

• docs/layers.md:352 -- 'Choosing SpecKit pulls speckit, speckit-beads, and steering-speckit together. speckit-beads is what connects SpecKit to bd.'
• docs/layers.md:304 and agentic/apm's apm.yml.jinja comment -- 'speckit when SpecKit is in use' as a recommendation agentic/marketplace would make.

So today, adopting SpecKit means an agent adds three locators to apm.yml's dependency list. There is no layer, no variables, no scaffolded structure, and nothing renders .specify/ or the workflow gates.

WHY A LAYER: an apm locator installs packages; it does not scaffold. SpecKit needs its own directories, its workflow gates, and the beads wiring, which is the same argument that made quality/hooks and host/github layers rather than package recommendations.

OPEN QUESTIONS -- the rearchitecture should settle these before the layer is written:

1. Layer name and group. agentic/speckit, or a group of its own?
2. What it renders: .specify/ tree, gate config, the /speckit.* command surface, or only the config with the commands still coming from the apm package?
3. Relationship to the apm packages. Does the layer replace the three locators, or render structure AND declare them? speckit-gate ships on PyPI, which is a third source.
4. Whether it depends on agentic/beads. speckit-beads connects the two, so the layer order matters.
5. Its variables. Bailiff's speckit-adjacent packages are not ported, so there is no prior answer set to reduce.

BLOCKED ON: the rearchitecture landing. Writing the layer against the current shape would be work thrown away.

Do not port or invent this layer until the new architecture is known.

title: Gitignore repomix output
description:
mcp-repomix's hook writes repomix.xml into the repo root, and neither platevault/.gitignore nor agentic-packages/.gitignore mentions it. The file is 4.7MB for agentic-packages and 39MB for platevault.

base/gitignore must exclude it, and any repo that already committed one needs it removed.
acceptance_criteria: repomix.xml and any variant the recipes emit are ignored in a rendered repo. No existing repo has one committed.
notes:
Covered by the brief at /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md, change 4.
WIDEN: --skill-generate writes .claude/skills/<name>/references/files.md, which holds every file's contents -- the same bulk as repomix.xml, but in a directory that looks like hand-authored config and is easy to commit by accident.

Ignore both: repomix.xml (and any variant a recipe emits) plus any generated skill directory. A generated skill carries a 'This skill was generated by Repomix' footer, so it is detectable.
close_reason: Already satisfied by agentic/index: .gitignore.d/index ignores repomix-full.xml, graphify-out/, .serena/, and all four repomix default output names including /repomix.xml. Verified in the shipped fragment.

title: Move the enforceable hooks into CI
description:
A local hook is advisory: --no-verify defeats it. Anything that must hold belongs in a CI job listed in the gate's needs.

Belongs in CI, from the audit:
- prek run --all-files (psc-7yy) -- the whole hook set, unbypassable
- attribution-guard over the pull request commit range (psc-f4q)
- close-keywords, checking the rewrite happened rather than that the message is clean
- the release-please guard: a hand-made version tag reaching the default branch
- conventional-commit format across the range, not just the tip

Stays local-only: formatters and fixers that rewrite files, since CI should fail rather than commit; and anything needing the working tree before the commit exists.

The split rule: a check that reads committed state goes in CI. A check that rewrites or inspects staged state stays a hook.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
close_reason: The enforceable checks are in CI. prek run --all-files was already there; what was missing is commit-range enforcement, since conventional-pre-commit runs at commit-msg (which --no-verify defeats) and sees only the message being written. New 'commits' job in wc-quality.yml reads the whole PR range with fetch-depth 0, skips forge-generated merge subjects, and refuses a hand-made version tag that no hook can see because a tag is pushed rather than committed. Verified against real commits and clean under actionlint and zizmor. 4 tests at 257f8b8.

title: Enforce that hooks ran, in CI
description:
prek has no way to check whether its shims were installed, and --no-verify always wins locally. Enforcement is therefore three layers, and only one of them actually enforces.

CI: 'prek run --all-files' as a job inside the quality workflow, listed in the gate's needs. This is the layer that cannot be bypassed.

Bootstrap: 'just setup' runs prek install, so a fresh clone gets the shims.

Branch protection: the gate as a required check with no bypass. Covered by psc-0sw.

The commit-msg and pre-push hooks exist for fast feedback. CI exists for correctness.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
close_reason: Already satisfied: 'prek run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure' runs in wc-quality.yml's quality job, which the gate needs, so the whole hook set is unbypassable. --all-files rather than a diff range, since a hook bypassed at commit time stays bypassed for files outside the range. Test added at 257f8b8.

title: Let language layers contribute to the shared quality and security jobs
description:
wc-quality.yml and wc-security.yml are language-blind, but the tools inside them are not: lizard needs per-language complexity config, CodeQL needs sec_codeql_languages, trivy differs between fs and config mode, and OSV depends on which lockfiles exist.

CodeQL's language names also differ from ours (javascript-typescript, not ts), so the mapping cannot live in the host layer.

Add a third contribution point: each lang/* layer drops .github/quality.d/<lang>.yml and .github/security.d/<lang>.yml as job fragments. The host layer's shared workflows carry the neutral steps plus a matrix the agent fills from the fragments.

GitLab needs nothing extra; the .gitlab/ci/*.yml glob already covers it.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
close_reason: Already satisfied and now enforced. Every lang/* layer ships .github/quality.d and .github/security.d fragments that the host layer's wc-quality and wc-security read at run time to build their matrices. Checking found lang/api missing its security fragment; added, stating codeql unsupported and trivy secret-scanning applicable. New invariant requires both fragments plus an explicit codeql claim. Discovery verified end to end. At HEAD.

title: Make the agentic layer marketplace-only
description:
Carried from bfsh-cvh. Do not install agent hooks or per-harness config directly, only through apm, claude, or codex marketplaces.

The layer ships no .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, marketplace.json, opencode.json, or kiro files. It offers to add marketplaces, discovers plugins, then recommends installs, and it runs last after everything else has rendered.

This is also why better-t-stack's mcp addon stays off: it writes MCP config for three editors, which conflicts with globally managed config.
acceptance_criteria: The agentic layer writes no per-harness config file. It runs after all other layers and reports what it recommends rather than installing silently.
notes:
The beads sub-layer must invoke: bd init --prefix

--non-interactive --skip-hooks --agents-template templates/agentic/beads/agents-template.md --skip-hooks is not optional. Without it bd init copies the ambient hook binaries from the configured core.hooksPath into .beads/hooks, repoints core.hooksPath at the copy, and stages 347MB. The copied arm64 slice was unusable and every commit failed with 'cannot execute binary file'. Also add a hooks/ line to .beads/.gitignore. The template supplies the AGENTS.md body; bd appends its own managed block below it. Same shape for any other tool that appends. CORRECTED: bd gets no block in AGENTS.md at all. It is already surfaced by ~/.claude/rules/40-beads.md (scoped **/*, fires everywhere), ~/.agents/skills/beads/ (global), and .codex/hooks.json (native hooks) -- plus a fourth pointer from apm compile in an apm repo. Its own block was 54 of 90 lines and restated the same five commands. Recipe: bd init --prefix

--non-interactive --skip-hooks --skip-agents, then ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md. AGENTS.md carries one line naming the prefix. Same test applies to every tool: a tool surfaced by a global rule, an installed skill, or a native hook does not also get a block. MARKETPLACES, verified against ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/. SEED: srobroek/agentic-packages, srobroek/slopvac, srobroek/vibe-hero. DO NOT SEED repomix or worktrunk. Both are already wrapped as apm packages that do strictly more: mcp-repomix adds a PostToolUse snapshot-refresh hook the 3-plugin marketplace lacks, and worktrunk-writer plus hooks-worktrunk add writer lifecycle, branch leases, and cross-runtime enforcement over the single-plugin marketplace. Adding them would give two sources for one tool. Third-party marketplaces present but not ours: claude-plugins-official, dev-browser, thedotmack/claude-mem. SPECKIT: choosing it pulls speckit, speckit-beads, and steering-speckit together. speckit-beads connects SpecKit to bd. MARKETPLACE SET FINAL: seed srobroek/agentic-packages and srobroek/slopvac only. Not vibe-hero. Not repomix. Not worktrunk. repomix: the MCP server is not worth it over the CLI, and the evidence is in our own package -- mcp-repomix's refresh hook shells out to the repomix CLI at scripts/repomix-refresh-snapshot.py:100, not to the MCP. So the useful part is CLI plus a hook, and the MCP adds a server for nothing. Consider renaming the package away from the mcp- prefix. The apm recommendation scan must propose token-savings whenever agentic/index renders with index_full_pack: true. That package's repomix-read-guard.py is what makes shipping a contents pack safe: it denies a whole-file read of repomix-full.xml on both Read and Bash, so 'cat pack' is caught as well, with a TOKEN_SAVINGS_ALLOW_PACK_READ=1 escape hatch. It also carries rtk-rewrite-guard.py and spill-tool-output.py.

Writes only copier's answers file; every forbidden per-harness path asserted absent (.claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, marketplace.json, opencode.json, .kiro/). Reports rather than installs, runs after the aggregating layers, detects from the tree rather than the answers files, and dedupes against apm.yml. 12 tests at 6a0b587.

title: Decide the GitHub repository governance surface
description:
Deferred from the 2026-07-29 design session, to dive into separately.

The configuration surface that is neither template file nor CI job: branch protection and rulesets, required status checks, merge queue, allowed merge types, auto-merge, issue and pull-request templates, CODEOWNERS, repository settings, environments and their secrets, organisation versus personal ownership, and which repository features to enable.

Some is API-only and needs gh api rather than a committed file, which decides whether it is a layer or a script.

close_reason: Settled with measurement. gh api repos/<slug> reports every merge and feature setting, a fresh repo returned zero rulesets and 'Branch not protected', and GitHub reads no committed file for any of it -- so the split is evidence rather than judgement. Files (CODEOWNERS, templates, health files) in host/github; API surface (protection, required checks, merge types, auto-merge, features) in scripts/repo_govern.py; owner and visibility asked; environment secrets never automated. gate is the only required check. Applied to srobroek/agentic-scaffold and verified through the API, then --check reported 'governance matches'. Recorded in rules/choices.md. 6 tests at aed5a4d.

title: Add the check target that renders every profile and builds it
description:
Render each profile into a temporary directory and run its own build: the workspace resolve, the install, the test command, the lint.

This is the test that would have caught all of the failures in docs/gotchas.md. A tree that renders is not a project that builds.

close_reason: scripts/render_profile.py plus 'just profiles-build', wired into 'just check' via the profiles validator. Both fixed in the layers, not just the profiles. All 13 profiles green at cadb825.

title: Add the docs/site and deploy layers
description:
Astro plus Starlight at docs/site, three dependencies, renders in any repo regardless of language. Not better-t-stack's starlight addon, which places it at apps/docs inside a TS monorepo.

Two deploy layers. docs/deploy-sibling is the default: a <name>.github.io repo holding source and building itself, per platevault. docs/deploy-split is for when docs/api-refs renders: the code repo builds and pushes rendered output over an SSH deploy key, per prompting-press.

title: Write the project-scaffold-steering skill and generator
description:
Generate docs/agents/ per docs/steering.md: one directory per concern, per-language leaves, content between BEGIN GENERATED markers, .apm/context pointers, then apm compile.

A pure function of files on disk. No prompts, no network, so CI can verify it.

Reads clippy/ruff/golangci/biome/oxlint/tflint configs, rendered workflows, release config, test dirs, and env keys. conventions.md and gotchas/* get created from the template seed and never rewritten.

Text outside markers survives regeneration. Every appended block in AGENTS.md is complete on its own: deleting any one block leaves the rest accurate, and every index row names a file that exists.

Pure function of the tree: reads justfile/.just.d, .mise/conf.d, each language's tool config, the workflows, release-please config, and env names. Both markers carry the block name (a bare END matched nothing and wrote an empty block while reporting success). conventions.md and unmarked files are never written; adding a language adds a leaf and one index row without growing anything. --check reports drift without repairing. 16 tests at HEAD.

title: Write the project-scaffold skill
description:
Interview the six questions from rules/choices.md one at a time, derive the rest, pick a profile, run the generator, render layers in order, then generate docs/agents/.

Managed through apm so it installs like the other skills. Target 120 lines.
acceptance_criteria: The skill renders each profile end to end without asking a question that rules/choices.md marks fixed or derived, and reports every file written and every command that failed with its output.
close_reason: project-scaffold skill shipped at 93 lines (target 120), as an apm package under packages/project-scaffold. Interview asks exactly six questions, names none the choices table derives, routes to profiles rather than restating layer sets. This repo now publishes itself as the agentic-repo shape: apm pack builds both catalogs, --check-versions reports project-scaffold--v0.1.0 [matches]. 18 tests at 257f8b8.

title: Build render.py, index.py, and the justfile
description:
render.py wraps copier: resolve a layer, run a precheck, render, report what was written. index.py walks templates/ and regenerates docs/INDEX.md so the skill never names a layer from memory.

The justfile carries new, add, render, preview, index, check, and lint. Target under 250 lines total across both scripts.

scan.py, probe.py, CONTRACT.md, the axis system, and the runbooks are not ported.
acceptance_criteria: 'just preview <layer> /tmp/t' writes nothing and lists what it would write. 'just index' is idempotent. 'just check' renders every profile and runs its build.

Layer metadata goes in a _scaffold block inside copier.yml rather than a separate file, since copier ignores unknown underscore keys and a second file could disagree with the questions beside it. Verified: preview writes nothing, render writes 9 files, _skip_if_exists keeps hand-written content across a re-render, index --check exits 1 on drift.

title: Write the profiles
description:
One file per profile naming its layer set, the destination per layer, and what varies inside it. Derived from a survey of 54 repos.

agentic-repo covers 17 repos and has no language layer, which the old catalog had no name for. rust covers 12, python 10, ts 7, rust+ts 3 (all Tauri), go 1.

Each profile crosses {lib, app} x {single, monorepo}.
acceptance_criteria: A profile exists for every shape in the repo survey. Each names its layers, its destinations, and the generator command that runs first.
close_reason: 13 profiles written under profiles/, one per shape in docs/architecture.md's generator table, plus profiles/README.md carrying the format and survey counts. Each names its layer set in render order, generator, fixed/derived answers, and build commands. scripts/profiles.py validates the set. All 13 render and build clean at cadb825.

title: Add the GitLab host layer
description:
Four personal repos carry .gitlab-ci.yml (amassist, auto-sa, nightwatch-esp32, nightwatch-tunnel) and more than ten work repos live on gitlab.aws.dev.

The host layer ships .gitlab-ci.yml ending in 'include: - local: .gitlab/ci/*.yml' plus the stages list. Each lang/* layer drops .gitlab/ci/<lang>.yml. No caller needs writing, unlike GitHub.

nightwatch-esp32 already uses the non-glob form and is the reference. GitLab jobs install toolchains through mise rather than setup actions.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered GitLab repo runs lint and test per language with no hand-written caller. Every layer's stage appears in the host layer's stages list.

Each lang/* layer drops .gitlab/ci/<lang>.yml and the glob resolves it. Tested in test_host_layers.py.

title: Clear 64 prose-gate errors from the updated vale ruleset
description:
The review-docs vale styles resynced on 2026-08-17 and brought stricter rules. 64 errors now fail `just lint` across 8 files, all pre-existing prose: AGENTS.md, docs/agents/conventions.md, docs/agents/env/index.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/layers.md, profiles/README.md, rules/choices.md, rules/ci-composition.md.

title: Add the workspace/moon layer
description:
The last unported workspace layer. docs/layers.md specifies it writes .moon/workspace.yml from a 'members' variable.

Bailiff has no moon package, so this is new work rather than a port.

OPEN QUESTION before building: what moon earns over the existing surface. The repo already
has just for tasks, mise for toolchains, and prek for hooks, and workspace/monorepo resolves
members through the manifest's own glob. moon's value is task graph caching and affected-only
runs across a large monorepo, which nothing here has demonstrated a need for.

Measure before porting: on a two-member workspace, whether 'moon run' beats 'just each
<phase>' by enough to justify a fourth task runner in the stack. If not, consider dropping
the layer from docs/layers.md rather than writing it.

Members come from the workspace manifest glob, so the 'members' variable should be derived
the way scripts/add_member.py derives it rather than asked.
close_reason: Built, not dropped. My first measurement was wrong: it tested caching on two independent sleep tasks, which is not what moon is for, and I miscounted mise and prek as task runners (they are a toolchain manager and a hook runner). Sjors corrected both. Re-measured on a three-member dependency chain: moon 0.10s with nothing changed and 1.24s for a leaf change, against 3.37s every run for the equivalent just loop, plus transitive invalidation and graph ordering that just cannot express. Layer generates moon.yml per member from the manifest glob and each member's own dependency declarations; all four layouts verified against moon 2.4.6 and the real compilers. 25 tests. Closed at a5d7b07.

title: Format the scaffold output where a generator leaves it unformatted
description:
Three of four language scaffolds fail their own gate before a line of real code exists. Each was found by running the gate, not by reading:

- cargo init: rust.missing_docs and clippy.pedantic both fire under CI's -D warnings on the generated pub fn. Both left out of the generated manifest.
- uv init --lib: writes a function into src/<pkg>/__init__.py, which non-empty-init-module rejects. A task splits it into core.py.
- bun init: writes index.ts with no trailing newline, which biome's formatter rejects. A task runs biome check --write once.

go mod init is the only one that produces a clean tree.

The pattern is now handled per layer, which means a fifth language will hit it again and nobody will know to look. Consider a shared post-render step, or at least a line in the layer contract saying to run the gate against the generator's own output before declaring a layer done.
acceptance_criteria: A new lang/* layer cannot land without evidence its generator's output passes the gate. Either a shared normalisation step exists, or the layer checklist requires the evidence.
close_reason: The invariant the acceptance criterion asked for. Each language layer already normalises its own generator output; what was missing is enforcement. test_a_language_layer_declares_how_its_generator_output_is_normalised requires every lang/* layer to declare its normalisation task and asserts the task is in the layer's _tasks. None is a positive claim the generator needs nothing, true only of go mod init. Verified the invariant fires against a probe layer. At d8ce6d1.

title: Nudge repomix --remote when an agent reaches for a remote repository
description:
hooks-package-investigate is the template: PreToolUse on Bash, regex-matched command patterns with a _BOUNDARY prefix, emitting hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext non-blocking.

Two triggers, and the second is the stronger one:

CLONE: r'(git\s+clone|gh\s+repo\s+clone|degit|tiged)(\s|$)'. repomix --remote <url> --remote-branch <ref> packs a remote repo with no working copy at all -- no disk, no cleanup.

WEBFETCH: matcher WebFetch, URL matching github.com/<owner>/<repo>. This is the moment an agent is about to read ONE file of a repo through a web page, when --remote would give it the whole thing structurally.

Compose with --skill-generate: it emits .claude/skills/<name>/ with SKILL.md plus references/{summary,project-structure,files,tech-stacks}.md, and the SKILL.md tells the agent to grep files.md for '## File: <path>'. So investigating a dependency leaves a durable browsable reference rather than a one-shot read. That is progressive disclosure over someone else's codebase, which is a better fit than snapshotting your own.

CAVEAT: --skill-generate prompts interactively for the output path unless both --skill-output <path> and -f are passed. A hook or recipe that omits either will hang.
acceptance_criteria: A git clone or a GitHub WebFetch surfaces the --remote invocation once, without blocking. The suggested command runs non-interactively. Silent for non-GitHub URLs and for a clone of a repo already local.
notes:
Brief at /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md, change 5.
GOTCHA in --skill-generate output: SKILL.md's usage examples are FABRICATED. Verified on a repo containing only src/lib.ts, package.json, and README.md -- the generated SKILL.md instructs the reader to look at src/index.ts (42 lines), src/utils/helpers.ts (128 lines), '## File: src/utils/helpers.ts', and 'function calculateTotal'. None exist; rg found no calculateTotal.

Only three lines are repo-specific: the frontmatter name, the description, and the H1. Plus a stats line. Everything else is a fixed template.

The references/*.md files ARE accurate: project-structure.md showed src/lib.ts (1 lines) correctly and tech-stacks.md identified Node.js from package.json.

So SKILL.md needs reviewing or replacing rather than trusting. An agent following it hunts for files that do not exist -- low harm, but noise.

Also: hooks-package-investigate is ours (Sjors Robroek, Apache-2.0, first landed 2026-06-26 in #370, ported to Python in #797). Its _BOUNDARY prefix and suffix-regex-per-verb-class shape is house convention, not borrowed, so copying it is copying our own pattern.
close_reason: Not project-scaffold work: this is an agentic-packages change, specified in full at /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md. This repo's repomix surface is the gitignore (psc-5ro) and naming the structural tool in docs/agents/index.md.

title: Drop the repomix MCP server, keep the CLI and the hook
description:
Every repomix MCP tool has a CLI flag, verified against repomix 1.17.0 --help:

pack_codebase          -> repomix .
pack_remote_repository -> --remote <url> --remote-branch <name>
generate_skill         -> --skill-generate [name] --skill-output <path>
read_repomix_output    -> Read on the output file
grep_repomix_output    -> Grep, or rg
file_system_read_file  -> Read
file_system_read_directory -> Glob
attach_packed_output   -> --output, --stdout

Two are strictly worse than the built-ins they duplicate: grep_repomix_output searches a stale snapshot where Grep searches the live tree, and file_system_read_file adds nothing over Read.

The cost is a stdio subprocess (npx -y repomix --mcp) plus eight tool schemas in every session's context. mcp-repomix's own refresh hook already shells out to the CLI at scripts/repomix-refresh-snapshot.py:100, so nothing in the package needs the server.

MIGRATION: nine apm.yml files depend on mcp-repomix, including ~/.apm/apm.yml -- agentic-packages, alm, claudebroker, demo, platevault, prompting-press, speckit-roadmap, vibe-hero. Removing the mcp: dependency block is a version bump across all of them.

The package keeps its refresh hook and gains the staleness check and the reminder, so rename it off the mcp- prefix.

title: Add context-pack recipes to the just surface
description:
The --include pattern is per-profile and derived from which language layers rendered, so it cannot live in documentation without drifting from the layout.

The docs/agents layer contributes .just.d/context.just with a pack recipe scoped by --include, a pack-code recipe adding --compress for languages where it earns its keep, and whatever the staleness hook should name.

Three reasons a recipe beats a documented command: the include pattern is generated from the rendered layers so it cannot drift; it shares the surface with just check, just docs:agents, and just add, so 'just --list' finds it; and the SessionStart staleness hook can name a recipe instead of a 120-character command line.

Owner is the docs/agents layer, which already owns the structural-tool choice and index.md.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered repo has a pack recipe whose --include matches its language layers. The staleness hook names that recipe. Adding a language layer updates the pattern.
close_reason: just pack-code added, with --compress, as a separate recipe rather than a flag on pack. Re-measured: compress cut this scaffold's python sources 27215 to 14321 bytes (47 percent, not the 21 the doc recorded) but GREW the jinja templates by 0.1 percent since it cannot parse them, which is exactly why it is not a flag on pack. repomix-code.xml gitignored. docs corrected with both figures. 2 tests at d8ce6d1.

title: Nudge agents toward the structural tool with a PreToolUse hook
description:
Steering prose alone does not hold: it is read once and lost after compaction. platevault's gitnexus instructions already try prose ('FIRST tool for where is X, use rg only for exact text lookups') and it is the only enforcement there.

hooks-serena is the precedent in agentic-packages: PreToolUse on 'Read|Grep|Glob|Bash' runs 'serena-hooks remind', with SessionStart activate and SessionEnd cleanup.

Apply the same to whichever structural tool the repo has, repomix or gitnexus. Non-blocking, through systemMessage rather than permissionDecision, because grep is the correct tool for an exact-text lookup and denying it would be wrong.

Enforcement ladder, weakest first: steering prose, SessionStart staleness check, PreToolUse reminder at the decision point. Denying grep sits beyond the useful end.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
notes: Covered by the brief at /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md, change 3. Precedent is packages/hooks-serena/hooks/claude-hooks.json, which splits claude-hooks.json from codex-hooks.json. Matcher is Grep|Glob only, never denies, rate-limited per session with SessionEnd cleanup holding the state.

title: Check snapshot staleness at SessionStart instead of packing
description:
A pack is 1.4s to 3.6s and repomix has no cache: two runs with identical arguments took 1.83s then 1.35s for the same token count. So packing at SessionStart costs every session 2 to 4 seconds for a snapshot that goes stale on the agent's first edit and may never be read.

mcp-repomix already writes a HEAD marker at <state>/<digest>.sha. SessionStart can compare 'git rev-parse HEAD' against it, which costs about 5ms, and say nothing when fresh or report how many commits stale when not.

Do not pack in pre-commit either. A pre-commit snapshot captures the tree being committed, but an agent needs one before it starts. The existing PostToolUse:Bash trigger already fires on git switch -c, checkout -b, worktree add, merge, pull, and rebase, which are the moments a stale snapshot starts to mislead.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (for an agent working in ~/personal/dev/agentic-packages, package packages/mcp-repomix).

MEASUREMENTS to re-verify, taken 2026-07-29:
- pack cost 1.4s for 1,269 files, 3.6s for 4,107
- NO caching: two runs, same args, 1.83s then 1.35s, identical token count
- --compress 21% on a 4,107-file Rust+TS repo; 0% on .md and .json which were 59% of bytes
- 197 of 4,107 files GREW under --compress; one 672-line .rs went 24,523 to 28,548 chars
- --include gave 81% packing code alone

WHAT EXISTS: scripts/repomix-refresh-snapshot.py as PostToolUse on Bash. Matches git (switch -c|checkout -b|worktree add|merge|pull|rebase), seven gates, packs detached via a self-reexec _pack subcommand. Writes a HEAD marker to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-tools/repomix/<md5(repo_root)>.sha with a lockdir beside it. Output at <repo_root>/repomix.xml. REUSE repo_hash() and that marker path exactly; the new hook reads what this one writes. Leave the seven gates alone.

THE HOOK:
1. Resolve repo root, exit 0 silently when there is none.
2. Read the marker. Absent means no snapshot: report that plus the command.
3. Compare against git rev-parse HEAD. Equal means exit 0, NO OUTPUT.
4. Different means report git rev-list --count <marker>..HEAD plus the recipe.

Never packs. Budget 5ms: two git calls, one file read, only sys imported at module scope per the existing script's header convention. Emit additionalContext, never a permission decision. Silence when fresh is the point.

DONE WHEN: fresh snapshot prints nothing and returns under 20ms; stale one names the commit distance and the fix; it never packs and never blocks. Tests beside tests/test_repomix_refresh_snapshot.py in its style. Worktrunk lease plus a PR, conventional commit subjects.

OUT OF SCOPE: packing at SessionStart or pre-commit (wrong moment, nothing to amortise). --compress as a default (per-language choice). The seven gates -- their premise that a pack is expensive does not hold, but changing them is a separate change.
Full implementation brief written to /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md. It covers four changes in order: strip the detached re-exec, lockdir, and 180s timeout from the existing hook; add the SessionStart staleness check; add the PreToolUse reminder; gitignore repomix.xml. Includes the measurement table to re-verify and the explicit out-of-scope list.
close_reason: Premise overtaken, concern addressed. The bead proposed a SessionStart hook comparing HEAD against mcp-repomix's marker, but this repo rejected that MCP server and stores no snapshot, so no marker existed. Instead: just pack writes the packed HEAD to repomix-full.xml.sha and just pack-check reports how many commits behind, measured at ~80ms against 1.4-3.6s to pack. Reports and exits 0 in every branch, since a stale pack is information rather than a broken build. All three paths verified; marker gitignored; the architecture doc's stale SessionStart row corrected. 3 tests at HEAD.

title: Generate a repomix snapshot in CI after merge
description:
agentic-packages' mcp-repomix already refreshes a snapshot locally on a PostToolUse:Bash hook after branch and integration events, gated on a clean tree and unchanged HEAD, and it shells out to the repomix CLI rather than the MCP server (verified: scripts/repomix-refresh-snapshot.py line 100 runs ['repomix','--style','xml','--output',...]).

A post-merge CI job gives every agent and every clone the same snapshot without each one paying the pack cost. Repomix packs whole rather than indexing incrementally, so a pack is expensive and doing it once per merge beats once per developer.

Open: where the artefact lives. A build artefact expires; committing repomix.xml churns every merge; a release asset or a branch outside refs/heads are the other options.

Compression matters: --compress cuts tokens by roughly 70 percent via tree-sitter, which suits a snapshot meant for agent consumption.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
close_reason:
Measured, and the premise does not hold. A full pack is 1.4s for agentic-packages (1269 files) and 3.6s for platevault (4107 files), so there is no cost for CI to amortise.

Storage makes it worse rather than better: a build artifact needs 'gh run download' plus auth and expires at 90 days, a release asset only exists at release boundaries, and an orphan branch needs an explicit fetch. Every one needs a fetch step the agent must be told about -- at which point telling it 'run repomix' is faster and never stale. A committed repomix.xml is 30-39MB churning on every merge and stale the moment anything lands.

Resolution: do not store a snapshot. docs/agents/index.md names repomix as the structural tool and gives the command. This is also why mcp-repomix shelling out to the CLI is the right shape and the MCP server is not.

title: Migrate the release-please guard to a pre-push hook
description:
release-please's PreToolUse:Bash guard catches manual 'git tag v1.2.3', tag pushes, and hand-merging a release branch to a protected branch, all of which strand release-please's autorelease:tagged label.

A tag push is exactly what pre-push sees, so the guard works there and then applies to every committer rather than only to agents.

It emits advice rather than a denial, per the repo hook policy, so the pre-push version warns without failing.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
notes:
VERIFIED: prek pre-push hooks work under git-defender. With core.hooksPath set repo-locally to .git/hooks, 'prek install -t pre-push' installs the shim and a push fires it -- observed 'pre-push probe.....Passed' on a push to a local bare remote. So the release-please guard can move to pre-push.

Caveat for the guard's own logic: git-defender intercepts pushes to github.com and requires 'dgit push' instead, so a pre-push hook sees the push attempt but the transport differs. Test the guard against both paths.

Priority raised from 3 to 2: pre-push is confirmed viable.
close_reason: Not project-scaffold work: this is an agentic-packages change, specified in full at /tmp/repomix-hooks-brief.md. This repo's repomix surface is the gitignore (psc-5ro) and naming the structural tool in docs/agents/index.md.

title: Run attribution-guard and close-keywords in CI as well as at commit time
description:
A commit-msg hook is bypassable with --no-verify, so the same checks belong in CI over the pull request's commit range.

attribution-guard: pipe 'git log --format=%B base..HEAD' through the vendored script. It pattern-matches authorship-shaped claims, so it reads a message the same way from either entry point.

close-keywords: in CI the check is whether the rewrite happened, not whether the message is clean, since the hook rewrites in place.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
close_reason: Superseded by the commits job added in psc-nnt. wc-quality.yml now reads the whole PR range for Conventional Commits with fetch-depth 0 and refuses a hand-made version tag. attribution-guard and close-keywords are agentic-packages hooks rather than layer content; when a repo installs them, prek run --all-files in the same workflow already covers them unbypassably.

title: Move the git-triggered agent hooks into prek
description:
Three agentic-packages hooks act on git actions and currently fire only for agents. As prek hooks committed to the repo they fire for every committer and for CI, and they survive an agent running without the global config.

hooks-close-keywords: already ships templates/pre-commit-commit-msg.yaml with a comment saying project-setup merges it and vendors the script. Rewrites 'Closes #1, #2' to 'Closes #1, closes #2' because GitHub binds a closing keyword to only the first issue. Ready to port.

hooks-attribution-guard: pattern-matches authorship claims in commit messages. A commit-msg hook catches these regardless of committer.

hooks-git-safety: only the force-push guard has a git hook to attach to (pre-push). reset --hard, clean -fd, and checkout -- are pre-execution guards with no git equivalent, so they stay as PreToolUse.

Not migratable: hooks-quality (PostToolUse on edits), hooks-bash-safety (guards arbitrary shell), hooks-worktree and hooks-worktrunk (no git events).
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
notes:
SCOPE CONFIRMED after auditing all 13 hook packages.

MIGRATE + DROP: hooks-close-keywords. Already ships templates/pre-commit-commit-msg.yaml with a comment saying project-setup merges it and vendors the script. Once ported, drop the package with a clear note in its CHANGELOG explaining the pre-commit hook supersedes it and fires for every committer, not only agents. Needs a worktrunk lease + PR against agentic-packages.

MIGRATE, KEEP BOTH: hooks-attribution-guard. Port to commit-msg AND add the CI check (psc-f4q). Keep the PreToolUse guard for pre-execution.

KEEP AS PACKAGE: hooks-git-safety. Only force-push has a git hook to attach to; reset --hard, clean -fd, checkout -- are pre-execution guards with no git equivalent.

ALSO FOUND: release-please's PreToolUse guard is migratable to pre-push (psc-1rk). steering-git-workflow's pr-create-guard is NOT -- gh pr create is not a git operation.

NO lifecycle hooks anywhere in agentic-packages: zero SessionEnd, Stop, SessionStart, or PreCompact across all 13 packages. Only bd has those.
close_reason: Three git-action hooks migrated to prek in .pre-commit.d/git-actions.yaml: normalize-close-keywords and attribution-guard at commit-msg, no-force-push-to-default at pre-push. Verified end to end through prek. attribution-guard needed a new entry point since upstream reads a PreToolUse payload and inspects the shell command while a commit-msg hook gets a file path; patterns vendored for their recorded false-positive fixes. Force-push guard compares ancestry, since --force is absent from the pre-push ref stream. Fragment records why the other ten stayed behind. 10 tests at 8b2c8be.

title: Replicate bd's five git hooks as prek entries
description:
Measured: bd init writes five ~1.3KB shell shims to .beads/hooks and repoints core.hooksPath. Each is identical apart from the event name: 'bd hooks run <event> $@' under timeout ${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-300}, guarded by 'command -v bd'.

Events: pre-commit, post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push, prepare-commit-msg. prek supports all five stages.

So the 347MB problem was git-defender's binaries being copied in alongside, not bd's own hooks. Five local prek entries reproduce the behaviour with no hooksPath hijack.
acceptance_criteria: --acceptance
notes:
TWO SETS OF HOOKS, both needed.

GIT hooks (reproduce in prek): five 1.3KB shims in .beads/hooks, each running 'bd hooks run <event>' under timeout ${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-300} -- pre-commit, post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push, prepare-commit-msg.

AGENT hooks (keep bd's own): four codex lifecycle hooks in .codex/hooks.json plus [features] hooks = true in .codex/config.toml -- SessionStart (startup|resume|clear), UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact (manual|auto), PostCompact (manual|auto), each running 'bd codex-hook <Event>'.

So --skip-agents must NOT be used: it kills the agent hooks that keep beads context alive across compaction, which is what makes dropping the AGENTS.md prose block safe. Use --skip-hooks alone, then replace the AGENTS.md body and symlink CLAUDE.md.
THIRD SET FOUND: bd also writes .claude/settings.json with a Claude SessionStart hook running 'bd prime --hook-json'. So bd installs three sets:

1. git hooks -- five shims in .beads/hooks running 'bd hooks run <event>' (reproduce in prek)
2. codex agent hooks -- four lifecycle entries in .codex/hooks.json running 'bd codex-hook <Event>' (keep as written)
3. claude agent hook -- .claude/settings.json SessionStart running 'bd prime --hook-json' (keep as written)

Note fd -H missed .claude/settings.json in the first pass; confirm with ls.

Done in 8c9e42f (quality/hooks) and extended in cdc549d.

Five prek entries in templates/quality/hooks/template/.pre-commit.d/beads.yaml, one per bd
event: pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, post-checkout, post-merge, pre-push. Each runs
'bd hooks run <event> "$@"' guarded by 'command -v bd', so a clone without bd still commits.

Confirmed prek 0.4.11 supports all five stages and 'prek install' writes a shim for each.
The stages also have to reach default_install_hook_types or the shims are never written;
merge_hooks.py computes that list from the fragments.

Added beyond the description: bd's own reference gives pre-push as 'runs chained hooks' and
it pushes NOTHING, so scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh was added at pre-push. Without it the issue
database stays on one machine.

comments.author: Sjors Robroek
comments.text:
Done in 8c9e42f, as part of quality/hooks.

Five prek entries in templates/quality/hooks/template/.pre-commit.d/beads.yaml,
one per bd event: pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, post-checkout, post-merge,
pre-push. Each runs 'bd hooks run <event> "$@"' guarded by 'command -v bd'.

title: Replace the hand-written commit-msg script with conventional-pre-commit
description:
hooks/baseline ships a 74-line check-commit-msg.py enforcing Conventional Commits.

compilerla/conventional-pre-commit (Apache-2.0, 544 stars, pushed 2026-07-20) does the same with real tunables: --strict disallows fixup! and merge commits, --force-scope makes scope mandatory, --scopes takes a comma-separated allowlist, and positional args replace the default type set.

It runs at the commit-msg stage, so the root config needs default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg].
acceptance_criteria: The hand-written script is deleted. A non-conforming commit message is rejected, and the allowed types and scopes are configurable from the layer.
close_reason:
Done in 8c9e42f.

compilerla/conventional-pre-commit v4.4.0 at the commit-msg stage, replacing the 74-line
script. Verified end to end against a real repo: a malformed subject, an unlisted scope, and
a missing scope each blocked a commit; an allowlisted scope committed.

--force-scope is only passed alongside --scopes: without an allowlist it demands a scope
while accepting any spelling of it, which is worse than not asking.

title: Wire bd's export-on-commit without the hooks hijack
description:
agentic/beads runs bd init --skip-hooks because bd otherwise copies the ambient git-defender hook binaries into .beads/hooks (347MB), repoints core.hooksPath at the copy, and produces an arm64 slice that cannot execute, failing every commit.

The cost is that bd's own git hooks are not installed, so its export-on-commit and post-checkout refresh never fire.

Options: run bd from a prek hook (prek installs into .git/hooks when core.hooksPath is set repo-locally, verified working), or file the copy behaviour upstream.
acceptance_criteria: A scaffolded repo gets bd's export-on-commit behaviour without bd rewriting core.hooksPath, and no hook binary is copied into .beads/.
close_reason: Superseded by psc-zpx, which measured what bd actually installs: five 1.3KB shell shims delegating to 'bd hooks run <event>', not the 347MB of git-defender binaries copied in alongside them. Replicating them in prek is five local entries.

title: Add API contract linting and breaking-change detection
description: Carried from bfsh-2v3. vacuum for OpenAPI linting and oasdiff for breaking-change detection on the api layer.
acceptance_criteria: A breaking API change fails CI. The lint runs on every merge request.
notes: Confirmed against the bailiff catalog: languages/api currently ships ONLY spectral (npm:@stoplight/spectral-cli in mise, one local hook running 'spectral lint openapi.yaml'). vacuum and oasdiff are not built. The layer should ship vacuum for lint and oasdiff for breaking-change detection, with spectral rendered only when a custom ruleset needs it.

Starter spec passes its own gate at 100/100 after adding four example blocks. Breaking change fails, additive passes, missing baseline does not block. 15 tests at 6a0b587.

title: Add per-language release tooling beyond release-please
description: Carried from bfsh-1p7. goreleaser for Go binaries, and the equivalent per language, alongside release-please for versioning.
acceptance_criteria: A Go project publishes binaries on tag. release-please still owns the version bump and changelog.
close_reason: release/goreleaser shipped. Division of labour: release-please owns version and changelog and pushes the tag; goreleaser reacts to it and attaches artefacts, with changelog.disable and release.mode append keeping them from colliding. Verified against 2.17.1: found the checksums/checksum key error via goreleaser check, and a real snapshot built 4 cross-compiled binaries plus checksums from one runner with ldflags version injection reaching the binary. cache: false on the release job, since zizmor reports caching there as cache-poisoning. Wired into go-app, not go-lib. 12 tests at HEAD.

title: Add opengrep security scanning with language-derived rulesets
description: Carried from bfsh-stz. opengrep rather than semgrep. The ruleset follows from which language layers rendered, matching the CI inversion.
acceptance_criteria: Each language layer contributes its own ruleset. The scan runs in the security job.
close_reason: opengrep shipped, meeting both criteria: each layer contributes its own packs via .github/security.d, and the scan runs in the security job on both forges. Verified opengrep 1.26.0 finds real command injection and gates correctly. Found and encoded a real trap: --sarif-output=FILE silently writes nothing while --sarif on stdout produces valid SARIF 2.1.0, so a workflow using the documented flag uploads an empty file and reports clean. title: Add the container layer
description:
Carried from bfsh-u95. Dockerfile, image build and push, image scan, plus hadolint (carried from bfsh-tvh).

Open before it can be written: base image policy, and who owns the Dockerfile when a framework generates one.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered container layer builds an image and scans it in CI. A base image policy is recorded.
close_reason: container/image shipped. Both open questions answered with measurement: base image policy is distroless (9.58MB/12 HIGH+CRITICAL vs alpine 16.8MB/12 vs debian-slim 143MB/34, and distroless carries no shell where alpine gives a compromise root plus one), recorded in docs/architecture.md and beside the FROM line. Dockerfile ownership: whoever wrote it owns it, both it and .dockerignore are skip_if_exists. Build-scan-push order enforced and tested. Real daemon build produced an 8.39MB image that runs as uid 65532 with no shell; trivy exits 0 on it and 1 on debian:11. 23 tests at 942b863.

title: Decide the better-t-stack default option set
description:
Verified option axes: frontend, backend, runtime, api, database, orm, auth, payments, addons, db-setup, web-deploy, server-deploy. Read at runtime from 'create-better-t-stack schema --name <name>'.

Proposed: tanstack-router, hono, bun, biome plus turborepo addons, starlight off since the docs/site layer supersedes it. Open: api is orpc or trpc, and whether database defaults to none.

Its validator reports incompatible combinations, so the skill can lean on it rather than encoding a matrix.
acceptance_criteria: A default recorded per axis, and a note on which axes the skill asks about rather than deriving.
close_reason: Settled against the real CLI. Every axis read from 'create-better-t-stack schema --name <axis>': frontend tanstack-router, backend hono, runtime bun, addons biome+turborepo. api=orpc, decided on evidence rather than preference: both scaffold the same apps/{web,server} shape within one dependency of each other (45 vs 44), but orpc ships @orpc/openapi and generates a server with OpenAPIHandler and OpenAPIReferencePlugin while trpc emits no OpenAPI at all -- so orpc is what makes lang/api's vacuum and oasdiff gates meaningful. database=none, verified accepted with api=orpc; it is an asked question per rules/choices.md since a CLI or static site needs none. Recorded in docs/architecture.md and profiles/ts-app.yml at 5b21385.

title: Decide the GitLab repository governance surface
description:
Deferred from the 2026-07-29 design session, to dive into separately.

The GitLab equivalent, which is a different model: protected branches and tags, merge trains, approval rules, CODEOWNERS, push rules, compliance frameworks, and project settings.

Applies to gitlab.aws.dev, where the instance version constrains what is available.

title: Add the cdk layer over projen
description:
projen owns the CDK and TypeScript build surface; the layers own CI, hooks, agentic, release, and license.

Set runner: TypeScriptRunner.tsx(), github: false, eslint: false. Bootstrap in order: projen new, install tsx, run npx tsx .projenrc.ts once directly, because the synth that would rewrite the ts-node task is the one that fails under TypeScript 7.

Gitignore entries go through project.gitignore.addPatterns().

title: Drop two dead guards from worktrunk-pre-start.py
description:
~/.local/bin/worktrunk-pre-start.py (165 lines, chezmoi-managed) carries six guards. Two cannot fire, verified against wt v0.68.0:

1. 'repository_root != worktree' -- worktrunk always passes a repository root. Created a worktree from a worktree and git rev-parse --show-toplevel equalled worktree_path exactly.

2. primary_worktree.is_absolute() and is_dir() -- wt step eval '{{ primary_worktree_path }}' returned /private/tmp/wtc from a nested worktree: absolute and existing. worktrunk resolves it.

The other four earn their place:
- has_tracked_cargo_manifest: the hook is global, so without it a Python or TS repo gets a .cargo/config.toml and an empty target/ for nothing. This is what lets the hook be global.
- is_tracked('.cargo/config.toml'): a project committing its own would otherwise be clobbered, showing dirty in every worktree.
- MARKER: an untracked hand-written config is invisible to is_tracked, so the marker distinguishes 'mine' from 'someone's'.
- EXCLUDE_MARKER: makes the .git/info/exclude append idempotent. Note that file is shared across worktrees, so it writes once per repo.

worktrunk has no cargo awareness: wt config create mentions only build = 'npm run build'. So target-dir sharing stays outside its model and the helper stays a file, in ~/.local/bin rather than a project layer, since it is per-developer environment.
acceptance_criteria: The two unreachable guards are gone and the helper is under 120 lines. The four remaining guards keep their tests. Behaviour is unchanged for a Rust repo, a non-Rust repo, and a repo committing its own .cargo/config.toml.
close_reason: Both guards re-measured dead against wt v0.68.0, deleted, four remaining paths verified end to end. Committed to chezmoi as 94678cbd.

title: Scope repomix packs with --include rather than --compress
description:
Measured on platevault, 4107 files: --compress cuts 10,365,446 tokens to 8,166,872, which is 21 percent, not the 70 percent claimed. Tree-sitter only compresses languages it has a grammar for, and .md plus .json are 59 percent of the bytes and pass through untouched (.md 0 percent, .json 0 percent, .rs -26, .tsx -65, .mjs -80, .py -68).

It also has a defect: 197 of 4107 files got BIGGER. crates/app/cache/src/lib.rs went 24,523 to 28,548 chars, +16 percent, because doc comments are duplicated around the elision markers and signatures are emitted more than once (38 'pub fn' compressed against 27 uncompressed). Comment-dense Rust is hit hardest.

--include is the better lever: code-only on platevault gave 2,009,042 tokens against 10,365,446, an 81 percent reduction with no defect, in 1.5s.

So the guidance in docs/agents/index.md should name an --include pattern per profile, and reach for --compress only when packing JS, TS, or Python source in isolation.
acceptance_criteria: docs/agents/index.md carries a repomix invocation scoped by --include for the profile. The compression measurements are recorded in docs/agents/gotchas/tooling.md.
close_reason: Folded into psc-buu: the --include pattern lives in the .just.d/context.just recipe that the docs/agents layer generates, so it is one deliverable rather than two.

The sibling repo nightwatch-nina-plugin holds only a LICENSE and a dependabot workflow.

Staying deferred per the bead's own description. One existing project that needs nothing is not the real need this was waiting for; the trigger is a NEW JVM or .NET project to scaffold.
